text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. When your application needs data from another service, it sends an HTTP request to a specific endpoint. The server usually responds with JSON, a lightweight format that is easy to read and parse. However, most APIs require authentication, often through an API key or token, to verify who is making the request. You must also respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can send in a given time. Finally, always include error handling in your code, because networks fail and servers return unexpected responses. Good error handling keeps your application stable.
